issues.legal_issue: Land excluded from transfer to a village body remains vested in the State unless the State later transfers it by a general or special order.
material_facts: A notification under the land-reform legislation specified that the relevant uncultivated land would not vest in the village body.
The State issued no general or special order transferring the land to the village body.
issues.conclusion: The land remained vested in the State, which therefore held the proprietary rights necessary to initiate the forest-land proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 6(a) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, estates and the rights of intermediaries vest in the State. Section 117 permits the State to transfer specified land, including forests, to a village body or other local authority by a general or special order; without such an order, the land does not vest in that body.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order: The proceeding is an appeal from a writ order concerning an entry in a land record.
predicates.land_excluded_from_village_transfer: A government notification excluded the land from vesting in the village body.
predicates.no_later_transfer_order: The State made no later general or special order transferring the land to the village body or another local authority.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a writ order concerns land excluded from village-body vesting and no later transfer order was made, the land remains vested in the State.

issues.legal_issue: A forest-initiation notification can satisfy the statutory description requirements by giving intelligible boundaries, while a later proclamation supplies parcel details.
material_facts: The notification initiating forest proceedings identified the total area and described its boundaries on all four sides.
A later local proclamation identified the disputed parcel by its land-record number as part of the notified area.
No objection was made to the proclamation.
issues.conclusion: The statutory procedural requirements for describing and notifying the proposed forest were satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 6 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 require the initiating notification to declare the decision to constitute forest land, specify its situation and limits as nearly as possible, and appoint a settlement officer. The explanation to Section 4 allows limits to be described by readily intelligible boundaries; Section 6 requires the proclamation to specify the proposed forest's situation and limits. The court found these requirements met on the facts.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_order and government_has_proprietary_rights and initiation_notice_gives_intelligible_boundaries and later_proclamation_identifies_parcels

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order: The proceeding is an appeal from a writ order concerning an entry in a land record.
predicates.government_has_proprietary_rights: The government held proprietary rights over the land when it initiated the forest proceedings.
predicates.initiation_notice_gives_intelligible_bou: The initial notice described the land's boundaries in a way that identified its limits.
predicates.later_proclamation_identifies_parcels: A later local proclamation identified the component parcels within the proposed forest.

issues.definition: When the government has proprietary rights and the initial notice gives intelligible boundaries while a later proclamation identifies the component parcels, the notification requirements are satisfied.

issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on acquiring rights over land covered by an initial forest notification applies even if no final forest-reservation notification has been issued.
material_facts: An initial forest notification covered the land before the claimed lease was granted.
The village body later purported to lease part of the land to the claimant.
No written grant or contract authorizing the lease was made by or on behalf of the State or a person in whom the relevant right was vested.
No final forest-reservation notification had been issued.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a final notification did not permit the village body to grant the lease or allow the claimant to acquire rights over the notified land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, as applicable in the State, bars acquisition of rights over land comprised in a Section 4 notification except by succession or under a written grant or contract made by or on behalf of the government or a person in whom the right was vested. In State of Uttarakhand v. Kumaon Stone Crusher, (2018) 14 SCC 537, the Court held that the relevant regulation operates after the Section 4 notification and is not defeated by the absence of a final notification under Section 20.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_order and initial_forest_notice_covers_land and later_local_body_lease and no_authorized_written_grant and no_final_forest_notice

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order: The proceeding is an appeal from a writ order concerning an entry in a land record.
predicates.initial_forest_notice_covers_land: A government notice initiating forest proceedings covered the land before the claimed right arose.
predicates.later_local_body_lease: A local body purported to lease the notified land after the initial notice.
predicates.no_authorized_written_grant: No written grant or contract authorizing the claimed right was made by or on behalf of the government or a person entitled to grant it.
predicates.no_final_forest_notice: No final notification declaring the land to be a reserved forest had been issued.

issues.definition: When a local body purports to lease land covered by an initial forest notice without an authorized written grant, the lease creates no right even if no final forest notice has issued.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue-record entry unsupported by a valid instrument does not establish title or a right to land covered by forest proceedings.
material_facts: The claimant's name appeared in a later land record as having possession of part of the land.
The earlier land records recorded the land as transferred to the forest department under the forest legislation.
No supporting written lease or other instrument creating the claimant's right was produced.
issues.conclusion: The claimant's revenue-record entry was inconsequential and created no right, title, or interest in the land.
issues.legal_principle: In Prahlad Pradhan v. Sonu Kumhar, (2019) 10 SCC 259, the Court held that revenue entries do not confer title and serve to identify the person liable to pay land revenue. The Court applied that principle here and held that an entry unsupported by the written instrument required to create the claimed right was insufficient.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order: The proceeding is an appeal from a writ order concerning an entry in a land record.
predicates.land_record_names_claimant: A land record names the claimant as an occupant or holder of the land.
predicates.no_supporting_title_instrument: No valid instrument supporting the claimant's asserted title or right was produced.

issues.definition: When a land record names a claimant but no supporting title instrument exists, the entry creates no land right.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory claim to land is not barred in consolidation proceedings merely because the government department did not object earlier when the claimant produces no instrument establishing a right to the land.
material_facts: The forest department sought correction of the land records on the basis of the land's statutory vesting and the forest notification.
The department had not filed objections in the earlier consolidation proceedings.
The claimant relied on a revenue entry but produced no written agreement establishing a right to the land.
issues.conclusion: The earlier absence of objections did not bar the forest department's claim, and the High Court erred in holding otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the land vested in the forest department by operation of the statutory notification and that the claimant had to establish a right by an agreement in writing made by a competent authority. A revenue entry alone did not do so. The High Court's reliance on Section 49 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953, to bar the department's objections was therefore erroneous.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and statutory_vesting_notice_covers_land and department_did_not_object_earlier and claimant_lacks_written_right_instrument

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The dispute concerns correction of land records in consolidation proceedings.
predicates.statutory_vesting_notice_covers_land: A statutory notification vested the land in the government department or otherwise formed the basis of its claim.
predicates.department_did_not_object_earlier: The government department did not object in an earlier stage of the consolidation proceedings.
predicates.claimant_lacks_written_right_instrument: The claimant produced no written instrument establishing a right to the land.

issues.definition: In consolidation proceedings, when a statutory notification supports the department's claim and the claimant lacks a written instrument establishing a right, the department's claim is not barred merely because it did not object earlier.
